name: Legging It

angles.text: Horde construction and resource gathering rely heavily on peons, so their routes need to stay safe.
Peons do much of the work in orcish settlements. Overseers rely on warriors to clear threats from their paths so work can continue.

faq.answer: Dangers along the road have frightened peons away from traveling south. Their duties wait until the way is safe.
The peons fear the dangers along the southern road. Without protection or a clear path, they refuse to travel to their assignments, bringing local work to a halt.
faq.q: Why were the peons afraid to travel south?

faq.answer: When the southern route is clear and immediate dangers are pushed back, overseers can send peons to gather resources and work in the field.
faq.q: What is accomplished by completing the task?

faq.answer: Peons are the Horde’s labor force. They harvest lumber, mine, and build fortifications. They are essential to settlements but poorly suited to combat, and readily retreat from danger.
faq.q: Who are the peons mentioned in the task?

faq.answer: The peons were traveling south along a path toward outlying work areas and resource deposits that need regular care. The journey had become dangerous enough to stop all traffic.
Peons lack military training and combat gear, leaving them vulnerable to wilderness predators and hostile forces. Overseers rely on experienced adventurers to clear threats and keep work routes safe.
faq.q: Why do peons require adventurers to clear their routes?

sections.body: Peons have left their assigned work undone and stopped traveling south. Perils along the road have made the journey too dangerous. Once the threats are pushed back, overseers can send their crews to work again.
sections.title: Securing the Line

sections.body: Peons do much of the Horde’s hard labor, from harvesting timber and quarrying to building outposts. They have little skill in battle, so roadside predators or hostile scouts can halt the movement of supplies. Clear routes keep settlements supplied and let the work continue.
sections.title: Labor and Route Security

summary: The peons have halted their southward travel because dangers line the road. Their work waits until the way is safe again.
